statement: Let M be a compact smooth Riemannian three-manifold with smooth, disjoint boundary components carrying constant Dirichlet values. For prescribed Z ∈ C1,b′ (M), 0 < b′ < 1, consider Ab(x, Z, Df) : Hessg f = Q(x, Z, f, Df), Ab = I + (b − 1)e ⊗ e, e = ∇f/|df|. (6.17) Suppose the actual coefficients extend smoothly at df = 0, are smooth on bounded ranges of their displayed variables, and the principal coefficient is independent of the height f. Suppose, uniformly on bounded input sets and any auxiliary compact parameter family, the following hold: 70 (i) constant upper and lower height barriers bound |f| ≤ M1 for every solution and for the normalized interpolation to ∆gf = c∗f, with fixed c∗ > 0; (ii) on that height range, 0 < b ≤ 1, b ≥ c/(1 + |df|), and |Q| ≤ C(1 + |df|); (iii) Qf > 0, uniformly away from zero on bounded variable ranges. Then the Dirichlet equation has a unique solution in C3,b′ . It depends continuously on the input and parameters and is bounded in C3,b′ on bounded input sets. No prospective floor condition on an implicit auxiliary variable is required.
